title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 25
paragraphs: So Darius spoke; and having appointed Artaphrenes—his own brother and son of his father—to be governor of Sardis, he marched away to Susa taking Histiaeus with him, after first naming Otanes commander of those who lived along the coasts. This man's father, Sisamnes, who had been made one of the royal judges, King Cambyses had killed and flayed because he had judged a case unjustly for money. After tearing away the skin, he had cut leather thongs from it and stretched them across the seat where Sisamnes had used to sit to give judgment; and having stretched them in the seat, Cambyses appointed the son of the Sisamnes he had killed and flayed to be judge in his father's place, charging him to remember in what seat he was sitting to pass judgment.
